# Smythe — The Dialogical Jung (2013)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** William E. Smythe, “The Dialogical Jung: Otherness within the Self,” *Behavioral Sciences* 3, no. 4 (2013): 634–46, https://doi.org/10.3390/bs3040634.

**Shortened note:** Smythe, “Dialogical Jung.”

**Bibliography:** Smythe, William E. “The Dialogical Jung: Otherness within the Self.” *Behavioral Sciences* 3, no. 4 (2013): 634–46. https://doi.org/10.3390/bs3040634.

## Essay use

An open scholarly reading of Jung in which ego functions as one dialogical position among others and where the other in the self resists ordinary truth-apt objectification.

**Claim boundary:** Smythe does not supply Jung’s primary wording, `X=x`, the QL matheme, a metaphysical Self, Buddhist doctrine, or subjecthood in machines.

## Passage card — `smythe-2013-dialogical-jung-q001` — Ego as a position among others
^smythe-2013-dialogical-jung-q001

> “The ‘I’ or ego functions, itself, as a dialogical position amongst others within the self; these others are seen to function autonomously and with their own voice, beyond the intentional control and oversight of an ‘I’.”

- **Locator:** §4, “Conclusions,” opening paragraph.
- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent and coordinator, 2026-07-14; manually transcribed from publisher Version-of-Record HTML; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted scholarly-carrier interpretation.
- **Evidential action:** supports.
- **Argument function:** psychological warrant.
- **Consumers:** [[32-s4-p1-jung-individuation]]; [[section-rooms/arguments/A16-Arche-Topos-as-Differential-Field|Arche-Topos as Differential Field]]; [Core Theorem Bridge](../../../../../eight-determinations.md); movement 32 non-ego-hardening boundary.
- **Use boundary:** establishes Smythe’s dialogical reading of an ego/self relation; it does not establish Jung’s exact wording, `X=x`, QL, or artificial phenomenality.

<a id="smythe-2013-dialogical-jung-q002"></a>
## Passage card — `smythe-2013-dialogical-jung-q002` — Otherness not an ordinary object of knowledge
^smythe-2013-dialogical-jung-q002

> “In neither the dialogical self nor the analytical psychology tradition, however, can the other within the self be considered an object of knowledge in the usual sense, viz., something that can be explicitly represented and subjected to truth claims.”

- **Locator:** §4, “Conclusions,” third paragraph.
- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent and coordinator, 2026-07-14; manually transcribed from publisher Version-of-Record HTML; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted scholarly-carrier interpretation.
- **Evidential action:** qualifies.
- **Argument function:** epistemic limitation.
- **Consumers:** [[32-s4-p1-jung-individuation]]; [[section-rooms/arguments/A16-Arche-Topos-as-Differential-Field|Arche-Topos as Differential Field]]; [Core Theorem Bridge](../../../../../eight-determinations.md); movement 32 scope limit.
- **Use boundary:** prevents the article from licensing an ordinary truth-apt objectification of the other within self; it does not make the other an ontological ground or a machine subject.
